cefrAlignment: Matches B2 (CEFR CV: can understand announcements and messages on concrete and abstract topics at normal speed, and recorded material in professional life): 140–195-word adverts, a news report and meeting talks with paraphrased options.
examFidelity: TOEIC Part 4 single-speaker talks with three questions (purpose/speaker, detail, next action), including a 'Why does the speaker say…?' item, follow exams.ts and real item styles; all questions follow the audio order.
fixes: Talk 2 explanation called the unnamed speaker 'she'; changed it to 'the speaker' so that nothing depends on the TTS voice's gender.
learnerOutcome: A learner can use the typical structure of adverts, news reports and meeting talks to predict when each answer comes, and avoid word-match and wrong-person distractors in TOEIC Part 4.
